O.outcome_detail: P1 amplitude difference between reversed and typical letters

cells.quote: Adults exhibited significantly greater differences between typical and reversed letters than children, who failed to exhibit significant differences between typical and reversed letters.
cells.note: The supplied study text reports the direction but does not print the P1 interaction effect size; the age-group comparison is nonrandom.

cells.quote: For the P1 component, adults had a significantly more positive going wave for reversed letters compared to typical letters than did children (group x condition interaction: F(1,22) = 5.19, p = .03, gp2 =. 1 9 ) . This interaction reflects the fact that adults showed a significantly more positive going amplitude for reversed compared to typical letters (F(1,22) = 6.96, p = .02, g 2 = .39), whereas children showed no reliable difference between these conditions on this component
cells.note: The detailed adult within-subject result is quoted from the wiki entry because it is not present in the supplied study-text excerpt; the printed effect size is therefore not taken from the study text.

O.outcome_detail: ERP scalp topography and source activity at 126–148 ms

cells.quote: The first significant period covariance map displays a topography marked by a negative potential at central sites, a positive potential at occipital sites, and a more diffused positive potential at fronto-temporo-parietal sites for increasedd’.
cells.note: The study reports a measured association between d′ and ERP topography, with source estimation implicating the precuneus (BA 7); no printed effect size for this association is provided.

O.outcome_detail: EEG ERP topography and sLORETA-estimated precuneus activity at 126–148 ms

cells.quote: The TANCOVA revealed two significant time periods (Fig.1a), the first at 126–148 ms and the second at 573–638 ms post-stimulus.
cells.note: Higher d′ covaried with a 126–148 ms topographic pattern whose estimated source implicated the precuneus (BA 7); this is an observational learner-difference association, not a causal treatment effect.

O.outcome_detail: EEG ERP topography and sLORETA-estimated frontal activity at 573–638 ms

cells.quote: The second significant period shows a covariance map displaying a topography marked by a positive scalp potential distribution over central regions for increased d’ (Fig. 1b, lower panel, with maximum value = 2.2 at electrode Cz; minimum value = −3 . 6 at electrode F7) . The sources associated with this periodcomputed with sLORETA are shown in Fig.1c (lower panel) and include the superior frontal gyrus (BA 11), with the highest activation at MNI coordinates X = −5, Y = 60, Z = −20, and to a lesser extent, the medial frontal gyrus (BA 6).
cells.note: Higher d′ was associated with a later topographic pattern and greater estimated frontal-source involvement.

O.outcome_detail: EEG global field power and sLORETA-estimated occipital activity at 322–507 ms

cells.quote: The GFP analysis revealed a significant positive association of the GFP with d’ at 322–634 ms (Fig.2a), indicating that stronger activation of active neural sources was associated with higher d’.
cells.note: The significant GFP interval was partitioned; the 322–507 ms effect was attributed to stronger participation of the middle occipital gyrus (BA 19) for higher d′.

cells.quote: In turn, practices P1 (21.6%), P2 (20.7%), P3 (18.1%), P4 (15.5%) and P7 (17.2%) were those with the highest percentages at the Redefinition level, that is, they indicate that ICTs made it possible to redefine them significantly.
cells.note: This is a descriptive percentage analysis of questionnaire responses, not an experimental comparison; no inferential test or direct treatment-versus-comparison analysis is reported. The comparison group is constructed from the remaining practices.
